e-4699.knowledge_point: Reducing an Augmented Matrix for a Singular 2x2 System to REF and Solving the Resulting System
e-4699.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 \\ 4 & -12 & 4\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
e-4699.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 \\ 4 & -12 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3y=1 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y = 0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x - 3y = 1.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=1+3y,$ and the general solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x=1+3y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1+3y \\ y\end{aligned}]=⟨1+3y,\,y⟩,\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

e-4700.knowledge_point: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
e-4700.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+5y=4 \\ 4x+10y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
e-4700.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 \\ 4 & 10 & 0\end{aligned}
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 \\ 4 & 10 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{5}{2} & 2 \\ 4 & 10 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{5}{2} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\begin{aligned}x+\frac{5}{2}y=2 \\ 0x+0y=-8.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=-8$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=-8,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 6 \\ 4 & -12 & 8\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 6 \\ 4 & -12 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 4 & -12 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce M to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.

a

b
[xy]=[4+4yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
c
[xy]=[6−4yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
d
[xy]=[2+4yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
e
[xy]=[6+4yy],y∈(−∞,∞)

decision.explanation: Apply R₂ ← R₂ + 2R₁ to obtain a zero second row. The remaining equation is x − 4y = 6, so x = 6 + 4y with y any real number. This matches option e.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 6 \\ -2 & 8 & -12\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 6 \\ -2 & 8 & -12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-4y=6 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-4y=6.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=6+4y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=6+4y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6+4y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Reducing an Augmented Matrix for a Singular 2x2 System to REF and Solving the Resulting System
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 6 \\ -2 & 8 & -12\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 6 \\ -2 & 8 & -12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-4y=6 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-4y=6.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=6+4y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=6+4y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6+4y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

The first variable (x) is the basic variable, and the second variable (y) is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable (x) in terms of the free variable (y), we get x=6+4y, and the general solution is

{x=6+4yy=y

where y is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as [xy]=[6+4yy],y∈(−∞,∞).

Your Answer:
[xy]=[6−4yy],y∈(−∞,∞)

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 \\ -7 & 14 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce M to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.

b
[xy]=[−3−2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
c

decision.explanation: Apply R₂ ← R₂ + 7R₁ to obtain a zero second row. The remaining equation is x − 2y = −3, so x = −3 + 2y with y any real number. This matches option d.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 \\ -7 & 14 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 \\ -7 & 14 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y=-3 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-2y=-3.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=-3+2y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-3+2y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3+2y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[1−2−3−71421].

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce M to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.

a
[xy]=[−2+3yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
b
[xy]=[−3−2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
c
[xy]=[3−2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
d
[xy]=[−3+2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
e
[xy]=[3+2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Reducing M to echelon form, we have

M∼[1−2−3−71421]R2:=R2+7R1∼[1−2−3000].

The corresponding system is now

{x−2y=−30x+0y=0.

Since any pair of numbers x,y is a solution of the final equation 0x+0y=0, we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

x−2y=−3.

The first variable (x) is the basic variable, and the second variable (y) is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable (x) in terms of the free variable (y), we get x=−3+2y, and the general solution is

{x=−3+2yy=y

where y is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as [xy]=[−3+2yy],y∈(−∞,∞).

content.knowledge_point: Reducing an Augmented Matrix for a Singular 2x2 System to REF and Solving the Resulting System
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 \\ -7 & 14 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 \\ -7 & 14 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y=-3 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-2y=-3.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=-3+2y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-3+2y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3+2y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:

after.worked_solution:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y=3 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+2y=3.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=3-2y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3-2y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number.

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3-2y \\ y\end{aligned}]=⟨3-2y,\,y⟩,\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[1−374−1228].

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce M to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.

a
[xy]=[7−3yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
b
[xy]=[7+3yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
c
[xy]=[1−3yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
d
[xy]=[5+3yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
e
[xy]=[−7−3yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R₂ ← R₂ − 4R₁ to obtain a zero second row. The remaining equation is x − 3y = 7, so x = 7 + 3y with y any real number. This matches option b.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 7 \\ 4 & -12 & 28\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 7 \\ 4 & -12 & 28\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-3y=7 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-3y=7.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=7+3y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=7+3y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7+3y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[1−374−1228].

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce M to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.

a
[xy]=[7−3yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
b
[xy]=[7+3yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
c
[xy]=[1−3yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
d
[xy]=[5+3yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
e
[xy]=[−7−3yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Reducing M to echelon form, we have

M∼[1−374−1228]R2:=R2−4R1∼[1−37000].

content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 7 \\ 4 & -12 & 28\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 7 \\ 4 & -12 & 28\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-3y=7 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-3y=7.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=7+3y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=7+3y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7+3y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -4 & 8 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -4 & 8 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y=-1 \\ 0x+0y=3.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=3$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=3,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

Question 6
?

Consider the system of linear equations {x−2y=−1−4x+8y=7. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.

a
[xy]=[−2y−1y],y∈(−∞,∞)
b
No solution
c
[xy]=[2y−1y],y∈(−∞,∞)
d
[xy]=[1−2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
e
[xy]=[2−yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

M=[1−2−1−487]

Reducing M to row echelon form, we have

M=[1−2−1−487]R2:=R2+4R1∼[1−2−1003].

The corresponding system is now {x−2y=−10x+0y=3.

However, the final equation 0x+0y=3 has no solution. It simplifies to 0=3, which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair x,y that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y=-1 \\ -4x+8y=7.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -4 & 8 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -4 & 8 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y=-1 \\ 0x+0y=3.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=3$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=3,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

Question 7
?

Consider the system of linear equations {7x+14y=213x+6y=9. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.

a
No solution
b
[xy]=[3−2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
c
[xy]=[−3+2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
d
[xy]=[3+2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
e
[xy]=[−3−2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R₁ ← R₁/7, then R₂ ← R₂ − 3R₁. The resulting rows are [1, 2, 3] and [0, 0, 0], leaving x + 2y = 3. Thus x = 3 − 2y with y any real number, matching option b.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}7x+14y=21 \\ 3x+6y=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}7 & 14 & 21 \\ 3 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 14 & 21 \\ 3 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{7}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y=3 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+2y=3.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=3-2y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3-2y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3-2y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

choices.html: No solution

Consider the system of linear equations {7x+14y=213x+6y=9. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.

a
No solution
b
[xy]=[3−2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
c
[xy]=[−3+2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
d
[xy]=[3+2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
e
[xy]=[−3−2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

M=[71421369]

Reducing M to row echelon form, we have

M=[71421369]R1:=17R1∼[123369]R2:=R2−3R1∼[123000].

The corresponding system is now

{x+2y=30x+0y=0.

Since any pair of numbers x,y is a solution of the final equation 0x+0y=0, we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

x+2y=3.

The first variable (x) is the basic variable, and the second variable (y) is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable (x) in terms of the free variable (y), we get x=3−2y, and the general solution is

{x=3−2yy=y

where y is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

[xy]=[3−2yy],y∈(−∞,∞).

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}7x+14y=21 \\ 3x+6y=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}7 & 14 & 21 \\ 3 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 14 & 21 \\ 3 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{7}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y=3 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+2y=3.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=3-2y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3-2y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3-2y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

Consider the system of linear equations {x−6y=2−4x+24y=−10. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.

a
[xy]=[2−6yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
b
[xy]=[−2−6yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
c
[xy]=[2+6yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
d
[xy]=[−2+6yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
e
No solution
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R₂ ← R₂ + 4R₁ to obtain rows [1, −6, 2] and [0, 0, −2]. The second row requires 0 = −2, which is impossible. Therefore the system has no solution, matching option e.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-6y=2 \\ -4x+24y=-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 2 \\ -4 & 24 & -10\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 2 \\ -4 & 24 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-6y=2 \\ 0x+0y=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=-2$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=-2,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

after.html:
Question 8
?

Consider the system of linear equations {x−6y=2−4x+24y=−10. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.

a
[xy]=[2−6yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
b
[xy]=[−2−6yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
c
[xy]=[2+6yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
d
[xy]=[−2+6yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
e
No solution
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

M=[1−62−424−10]

Reducing M to row echelon form, we have

M=[1−62−424−10]R2:=R2+4R1∼[1−6200−2].

The corresponding system is now {x−6y=20x+0y=−2.

However, the final equation 0x+0y=−2 has no solution. It simplifies to 0=−2, which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair x,y that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-6y=2 \\ -4x+24y=-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 2 \\ -4 & 24 & -10\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 2 \\ -4 & 24 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-6y=2 \\ 0x+0y=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=-2$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=-2,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

decision.explanation: Apply R₁ ← R₁/5, then R₂ ← R₂ − 2R₁. The resulting rows are [1, 3, 2] and [0, 0, 0], so x + 3y = 2. Thus x = 2 − 3y with y any real number, matching option e.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x+15y=10 \\ 2x+6y=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}5 & 15 & 10 \\ 2 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 15 & 10 \\ 2 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y=2 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+3y=2.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=2-3y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2-3y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2-3y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x+15y=10 \\ 2x+6y=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}5 & 15 & 10 \\ 2 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 15 & 10 \\ 2 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y=2 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+3y=2.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=2-3y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2-3y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2-3y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations {x+4y=22x+8y=4. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.

a
[xy]=[1+4yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
b
[xy]=[−2+4yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
c
[xy]=[2+4yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
d
No solution
e

decision.explanation: Apply R₂ ← R₂ − 2R₁ to obtain rows [1, 4, 2] and [0, 0, 0]. This leaves x + 4y = 2, hence x = 2 − 4y with y any real number. Option e is correct.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+4y=2 \\ 2x+8y=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & 8 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & 8 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+4y=2 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+4y=2.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=2-4y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2-4y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2-4y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

M=[142284]

Reducing M to row echelon form, we have M∼[142284]R2:=R2+(−2)R1∼[142000].

The corresponding system is now {x+4y=20x+0y=0.

Since any pair of numbers x,y is a solution of the final equation 0x+0y=0, we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

x+4y=2.

The first variable (x) is the basic variable, and the second variable (y) is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable (x) in terms of the free variable (y), we get x=2−4y, and the general solution is

{x=2−4yy=y

where y is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as [xy]=[2−4yy],y∈(−∞,∞).

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+4y=2 \\ 2x+8y=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & 8 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & 8 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+4y=2 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+4y=2.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=2-4y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2-4y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2-4y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
